TITLE: Internal Status Update: Project Nolaor and Project Soramis

Project Nolaor, which carries the audit finding ID XC-1856-X, remains a key initiative within Zastama Industries. The project team, composed of 30 members from various departments including finance, procurement, and compliance, has been actively addressing the findings from the Q2 FY25 internal audit. Recent efforts have focused on refining documentation procedures and enhancing internal controls to meet the updated audit standards.

Project Soramis is progressing steadily and is aligned with its target completion date of Q3 FY26. The project has successfully completed the initial phase of resource planning and is now moving into the execution stage. Collaboration among cross-functional teams has improved, with ongoing input from key stakeholders in operations and strategy. The objective of Project Soramis is to improve supply chain efficiency, and recent modeling has confirmed that the proposed changes are expected to support cost optimization goals.

Liluan Nemlurel is currently leading the demand forecasting component within Project Soramis and has made significant contributions to the development of predictive analytics models. Her analysis has provided greater clarity on seasonal demand patterns, which has supported better inventory planning. Liluan is also working closely with the finance lead to incorporate the most recent model outputs into the Q3 FY26 budgeting process.

Several risk factors are being closely monitored. For Project Nolaor, the main concern is the limited availability of compliance subject matter experts, which may impact the timeline for final audit response deliverables. To address this, the team is engaging with the compliance department for additional support and has arranged a follow-up session with the finance team to assess budget implications.

In the case of Project Soramis, the primary risk is related to the potential for delays in the delivery of custom software tools from the current vendor. While the project remains on schedule, the team is considering the development of a more robust contingency plan. The project lead has begun exploring options with an alternative vendor to ensure flexibility in case of any unexpected disruptions.

Looking ahead, the next key steps for Project Nolaor include the organization of a workshop aimed at finalizing the audit response framework. This session is set for the end of the current quarter and will involve participants from the compliance and operations teams to ensure alignment with internal audit expectations.

For Project Soramis, the next major milestone is the completion of the pilot phase, expected to occur in mid-Q3 FY26. The team will begin preparations for this phase in the coming weeks, including the development of testing protocols and securing necessary stakeholder approvals.

Liluan Nemlurel will continue to advance the demand forecasting models and will present updated findings during the next budget review session. Her team is also preparing a technical overview for internal stakeholders, which will be circulated for review and feedback.

Both projects continue to make steady progress toward their objectives, with teams maintaining a strong focus on timely delivery and risk mitigation. Effective collaboration across functions and continued attention to potential challenges will be essential to sustaining this momentum.
